sentences.text: Plesiocathartes is an extinct genus of birds belonging to the order Leptosomiformes.
The genus was originally described by Gaillard in 1908, with Plesiocathartes europaeus serving as the type species — the species a genus is based on.
Five species are currently recognized within the genus, including P. gaillardi, P. major, P. insolitipes, P. kelleri, and P. wyomingensis.
There are four recorded fossil occurrences in the Paleobiology Database, including finds of P. insolitipes at Walton-on-the-Naze in the London Clay Formation of southeastern England.
These birds lived from the Ypresian to the Rupelian stages, approximately 56 to 27.3 million years ago, with fossils found in Europe and North America.
